Entraining shallow-water layer

Words: 36
Reduced gravity OurBigBook.com
An entraining shallow-water layer changes depth, density, and momentum as ambient fluid crosses its interface. Entrainment dilutes its reduced gravity and accelerates or decelerates it through the momentum needed to bring new fluid into the layer.

Gravity current

Words: 4k Articles: 78
Reduced gravity OurBigBook.com
A gravity current is a predominantly horizontal flow driven by a density difference. Its front speed scales as the square root of reduced gravity times current depth.

Gravity current OurBigBook.com
For a one-sided fixed-volume gravity current in a unit-width channel with a closed rear wall, use front closure L˙=Fg′hf​​ with 0<F<2. An exact late-time similarity solution has u=L˙x/L, h=hf​[1−F2/4+(F2/4)(x/L)2] and hf​L=V/(1−F2/6). Substituting into the shallow water equations proves the radius law. The Benjamin deep-ambient front condition has F=2​. The virtual time origin tv​ is fixed by matching to the finite release, not by volume alone.

In a prismatic triangular channel with constant reduced gravity, the wave speed is c=g′h/2​ and the Riemann invariants are u±4c. The fan has c=(4c0​−x/t)/5 and u=4(c0​+x/t)/5, extending from x/t=−c0​ to uf​−cf​; a uniform region then reaches the front x/t=uf​. At​+(Au)x​=hwe​,(Au)t​+(Au2+g′h3/6)x​=0,(Ag′)t​+(Aug′)x​=0.
(1)

Floating extensional viscous gravity current (ht​+(hu)x​=0,4μ(hux​)x​=ρg′hhx​)

Words: 138 Articles: 1
Gravity current OurBigBook.com
A thin layer of very viscous liquid floating on an effectively inviscid denser liquid has negligible shear traction on both faces. Its leading horizontal velocity is a plug, and incompressibility gives vertical strain wz​=−ux​. Normal-stress balance shifts the pressure by −2μux​, so the longitudinal excess stress is 4μux​. Combining depth-integrated momentum balance with hydrostatic reduced gravity gives the displayed extensional equations. This is distinct from a no-slip, shear-driven thin-film gravity current.

V-shaped channel gravity current ((h2)t​=C(h4hx​)x​)

Words: 276 Articles: 3
Gravity current OurBigBook.com
For a fixed half-angle 0<α<π/2, a slow slender gravity current in a V-shaped channel has an almost horizontal free surface across each section. Its area is h2tanα, and its axial volume flux is −gQ(α)h4hx​/ν. Here Q is the integral of the dimensionless cross-sectional Poisson equation solution: Δϕ=−1, with zero velocity on the two rigid slopes and zero normal velocity derivative on the horizontal shear-free surface. Conservation of mass gives C=gQ/(νtanα). This treats the full two-dimensional section and does not require a shallow V angle.

Shear-driven viscous gravity current (ht​+A(h2)x​=D∇⋅(h3∇h))

Words: 195 Articles: 2
Gravity current OurBigBook.com
A thin dense gravity current on a rigid no-slip substrate can be carried downstream by imposed upper shear stress τ. For density contrast Δρ, lubrication theory gives q=Ah2ex​−Dh3∇h, where A=τ/(2μ) and D=Δρg/(3μ). The continuity equation gives the displayed equation. Besides small slopes and reduced inertia, the hydrostatic reduction requires τ/(ΔρgL)≪1 to keep shear-related normal stress small. Finite zero-thickness fronts are formal outer profiles and need a separate local description when their slopes are large.

Hydraulic control

Words: 516 Articles: 7
Froude number OurBigBook.com
A hydraulic control is a critical section where a shallow water flow passes smoothly between subcritical flow and supercritical flow. One long-wave characteristic speed relative to the bed vanishes there. Regularity supplies an extra relation between discharge, depth and channel geometry, allowing the control to set the discharge or upstream state. A critical depth alone is not sufficient for a regular transcritical solution: the channel forcing must also be compatible there.
Weir
Words: 107 Articles: 1
Hydraulic control OurBigBook.com
A weir is an obstruction across a channel that can regulate volume flux by creating a hydraulic control. In a shallow water model a sufficiently smooth crest has a critical section, with upstream flow subcritical and downstream flow supercritical under free discharge. Losses, submergence and geometry determine whether this ideal control applies.

Hydraulic control OurBigBook.com

Two successive hydraulic controls
Words: 90
Hydraulic flow in an inverted channel OurBigBook.com
For two same-height throats carrying the same light-layer volume flux and reduced gravity, the narrower throat has the larger critical minimum energy. A narrower downstream throat can back up and submerge an upstream throat. If the first throat is narrower, it can control discharge and feed a supercritical current through the second; a hydraulic jump followed by a second control is also possible when the available energy drop and intermediate geometry permit it. Equal throat widths are a marginal lossless case. Relative width alone does not fix jump position or mixing in the intervening reservoir.

Hydraulic control OurBigBook.com

On a flat bed a regular control requires a positive local maximum of q=Q/b. In the parabolic-width channel b=b0​(1+x2/L2), this maximum occurs at xc​=−SL2/(Q0​+Q02​+S2L2​), with qc​=(Q0​+Q02​+S2L2​)/(2b0​). Its critical depth is (qc2​/g)1/3. A control exists only when the prescribed total head equals the maximum critical-head envelope and the reach includes that point while retaining positive discharge.

Hydraulic control OurBigBook.com

In an ideal Boussinesq gravity current advancing beneath a much deeper ambient, the local head Froude number is uf​/g′hf​​=2​. The ambient must be displaced around the finite-depth head. This differs from the Saint-Venant dry-front condition, which neglects ambient inertia. The coefficient belongs to the ideal deep-ambient head model; confinement, mixing and drag can change it.

The momentum conservation equation is (Q2/h+g0′​ϕh2/2)′=−Wu if the withdrawn fluid carries its local horizontal velocity. Consequently uu′+g0′​ϕh′+g0′​hϕ′/2=0. At W=0, ϕ=e−Vx/Q0​ and the momentum flux is constant.
